notes: Classes are mutually exclusive. Record counts reproduce the frozen legacy algorithm, not clinical measurement cycles. MAP, mean arterial pressure; NIBP, noninvasive blood pressure.

Pairing used the median arterial MAP within -30 to +30 s and at least 80% valid reference coverage. Counts describe paired algorithm records, not authenticated measurements. MAP, mean arterial pressure.

values: SBP or DBP changed without MAP change
Does not prove no true measurement

The paired-record comparator is the median arterial MAP within -30 to +30 s, with at least 80% valid reference coverage. It is separate from the completed pre-adjustment bins used in infusion analysis.

Full channel-level diagnostics and field definitions are retained in workbook sheets Legacy_S09 to Legacy_S12 in Supplemental Digital Content 2. MAP, mean arterial pressure; NIBP, noninvasive blood pressure; SBP, systolic blood pressure; DBP, diastolic blood pressure.

name: Supp_Table_S06
title: Supplementary Table S6. Case-level variation under a 5 min display

notes: Mean arterial pressure threshold: 65 mmHg. Each case contributes one average across 30 sampling phases. Area ratios require positive reference deficit area; 42 zero-area cases remain in absolute state-discordance summaries. State discordance excludes display-unavailable time. Case summaries are not pooled exposure ratios. Among 1899 cases with ≥60 s episodes, the miss fraction was 36.7% [24.8 to 50.2%], with 5th to 95th percentiles 3.3 to 70.0%; within-case phase range was 66.7 [50.0 to 100.0] percentage points. Aggregate quantiles are in the workbook; case-level trajectories are not redistributed.

name: Supp_Table_S09
title: Supplementary Table S9. Display information at infusion adjustments and event-definition sensitivity

panels.label: a. Display states and persistence by sampling interval
notes: Low reference denotes MAP below 65 mmHg. Display states use 236 low-reference events in 85 cases from 83 subjects and sum to 100% before rounding. They describe the adjustment instant, not detection at any time during the whole episode reported in Table 3. Recovery persistence is averaged over all 184 events with confirmed recovery (80 cases, 78 subjects), with equal weight per event after averaging all sampling phases. Normal or unavailable display at recovery confirmation contributes 0 min. Persistence is restricted to the remainder of the 5 min post-adjustment window and terminates at normal display, missing reference or recurrent hypotension. CIs use subject-cluster resampling. A normal emulated display was not what the treating team necessarily saw. CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

panels.label: b. Fixed event-definition sensitivities at 5 min
values: At least 30 s preceding low MAP
notes: MAP threshold 65 mmHg, 5 min display. Each rule changes one feature of the primary analysis. One event per subject is selected by case identifier then relative time; chronological surgery order is unavailable. Equal subject weighting first averages events within each subject. These are descriptive sensitivity estimates, not treatment-effect comparisons. CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

Early-adjustment exclusion removes adjustments before 10 min from analytic-window start without masking the reference trajectory; it differs from startup-window masking measured from the first finite reference MAP.

name: Supp_Table_S11
title: Supplementary Table S11. Sequential and sensitivity associations with postoperative AKI

panels.label: a. Hidden-burden presence and sequential absolute-burden models
values: Absolute hidden burden, clinical plus reference burden
notes: *Two-sided Fisher exact test. The binary regression effect was not estimated because the no-hidden-burden group had zero AKI events. Four context-incompatible source-recorded ASA=6 values were treated as missing in primary adjusted models. Absolute hidden burden included zero reference AUC. Modified Poisson models used subject-cluster robust variance. These post hoc estimates are exploratory and noncausal. AKI, acute kidney injury; ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; RR, relative risk.

panels.label: b. Secondary compositional and sensitivity models
values: At least two postoperative creatinine values
notes: All models adjusted for the clinical covariates and nonlinear total reference hypotension burden specified in the main Methods and used subject-cluster robust variance. AUC, area under the deficit curve; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

name: Supp_Table_S12
title: Supplementary Table S12. Sequential associations with postoperative ICU stay of at least 2 days

notes: Absolute hidden burden was scaled per 10 mmHg min h-1. Primary adjusted models treated four context-incompatible source-recorded ASA=6 values as missing. The final model additionally used a three-degree-of-freedom spline of log(1 + total reference AUC per anaesthesia-hour). Modified Poisson models used subject-cluster robust variance. Analysis-plan-defined stability criteria required convergence, finite positive confidence limits, at least five events per parameter, and a CI width ratio no greater than 10. VitalDB does not distinguish planned from unplanned ICU admission; this is a supplementary resource-use association. ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; ICU, intensive care unit; RR, relative risk. All three models met these numerical stability criteria.

name: Supp_Table_S14
title: Supplementary Table S14. Cohort retention and episode visibility under startup quality rules

values: Cases affected by masking or window exclusion
Removed valid-reference time before coverage exclusions, min
notes: In the first 600 s after first finite reference MAP, flag 10 s bins with numeric MAP <40 mmHg, waveform coverage >=80% and p95-p05 <=5 mmHg. Sustained masking requires >=60 s consecutively flagged; all-bin masking has no run-length requirement. Both reapply >=80% whole-window reference coverage. Cases without source waveforms remain. Window exclusion retains the original cohort and can remove true early hypotension. These were algorithmic sensitivity rules.

Affected cases and removed valid-reference time are counted before coverage exclusions. Results use MAP <65 mmHg, a 5 min display and 30 phases; episodes require >=60 s of continuous finite low MAP. Parentheses give 95% subject-cluster percentile CIs (1000 replicates). The final three rows are mutually exclusive and sum to 100% before rounding. Original grids and phases remain; masked values cannot update sampling, and missing reference breaks episodes. AUC, area under the deficit curve; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

name: Supp_Table_S15
title: Supplementary Table S15. Infusion-adjustment results under startup quality rules

notes: Values in parentheses are 95% subject-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals (2000 replicates). Infusion event definitions, local pre-adjustment support and recovery rules are unchanged. The denominator for display states is the low-reference adjustment count in each column. Startup-window exclusion masks reference values for 600 s from the first finite reference MAP and then re-evaluates event support; it is not the early-adjustment exclusion from analytic-window start in Table S9b.

Persistence averages all confirmed recovery events after phase averaging. Normal or unavailable display at recovery contributes zero; lack of recovery is not assigned zero. The duration is restricted to the remainder of the 5 min post-adjustment window. Rules are defined in Table S14.
